reviews.title: Amazing case needs a couple tweaks.
reviews.comment: I love this case! It is a great size and the 90 degree rotation of the motherboard is awesome. I bought this case because of my belief that hot air from my GPU shouldn't rise up to my CPU. I'm not a professional PC builder and do minimal overclocking, so I work with what I can afford. I also live in a warmer region so the least amount of warm air in my case I can get, that's what I'm going to do. It fits my Tomahawk B550 MAG perfectly! Plenty of cutouts for cables to come through reducing the jumbled mess blocking airflow. I love how the I/O panel is on the top as well for looking down. The case comes with quite a few velcro straps for cables also. The only real problem I have with the case is that the CPU power cable has to do one of two things: either run down the back and out a cutout then back up to the plug, or use a vent hole for the PSU to slide the connector through. I chose the second option to reduce cord from running further length. Works and still looks pretty clean! Great case for a new look. Highly recommend!
reviews.author: Mr. K

reviews.title: Unique case, smaller than some full ATX cases, yet fits everything.
reviews.comment: I bought this case almost a year ago.  I was at first skeptical by the lack of reviews but the case definitely is a premium case. I did want a case where the GPU doesn’t sag, and I wasn’t sure if my 360mm radiator would fit. If you see in the 2nd picture I was able to mount my Arctic Liquid 360mm radiator without modifications through the top and back behind the GPU. Since the motherboard has a 90degree turn with the rear I/O facing upwards, it’s very easy to connect all your accessories. The only mod I added was buying rubber furniture raisers so that the four bottom fan pulls enough air into the case. No drilling necessary the bottom is flat, 3M double sticky tape did the job. The negative I could see is that the glass is pretty dark (also can be a positive since you see much of the cable management inside the case). The case is definitely heavy, but I was aware of that since this was a fully new build PC. PC Parts used: CPU - Intel i7-13700k (no issues) AiO - Arctic Liquid Freeze 360mm RGB MSI MPG Z690 Edge DDR5 M-Board G.Skill Trident Z5 RGB 48GB-DDR5-6800 RAM Zotac Trinity OC RTX4080 GPU (big card) Samsung 980pro 1TB OS Win10pro drive NVMe Samsung 980pro 2TB game drive NVMe Samsung 970evo 500GB file backup NVMe MSI 482 pro 2TB Picture/ video drive NVMe Samsung 850evo 500GB OS Ubuntu SSD 5x Noctua 120mm fans Samsung G8 34in OLED 175hz primary Alienware 34in IPS 120hz secondary

reviews.title: slightly unconventional case. looks sharp.
reviews.comment: wanted a slightly less conventional PC case that was mostly for an aesthetic i liked. the airflow with the availability of fan configuration looks a little unconventional upon quick observation. the back (glass) panel & compartment for wires is somewhat tight for how big the case is. it's fine, you will need to ziptie or velcro things together to get the glass panel on comfortably with a little more attention to wire management. the front compartment holds the power supply, typically where 3 or 4 fans would go in an open face, instead. the power supply compartment is probably oversized but that is okay because it leaves room for stuffing the extra wire length for the motherboard and gpu. i ended up placing a 3 fan CPU cooler + radiator on the back side, 1x 140mm fan on the top and 3x 140mm fans on the bottom. i'm running an AM4 with a 9070xt, which run a little warmer than nvidia cards and a Ryzen 7 5800XT, also a tad warm. configured the fans in bios to run a little more aggressively because of those factors. with the nominal suggested or average temperatures; both CPU and GPU run on the very coolest side. one thing i did do out of caution was 3d print feet to raise the entire case off the ground since the 3x 140mm fans on the bottom are doing most of the 'PUSH' for the airflow since it only has 1 top fan doing the 'PULL'. the 3x fans on the back run through the water cooled radiator and the GPU blows onto it, as well. they're doing a bit of heavy lifting. all-in-all, looks cool and doesn't seem to have any issues with the available airflow options.
